podcast-dannyjones-7HCnMJxw7JY:
Retired game warden John Nores warns Danny Jones about cartel crime and Chinese support. Nores spent years fighting illegal grows on wild land. He now speaks out after leaving field work.

He says cartels moved from weed into fentanyl, meth, and human smuggling. He calls the problem national, not just a border issue. The title warns that China handed cartels a game-changing tool. Nores ties drugs, poisoned land, and foreign help into one threat. The episode suits listeners who follow border crime and want a field officer's view. His voice is that of a man still sounding alarms.
podcast-dannyjones-qrK8W2OyWJY:
Demonologist Nathaniel Gillis joins Danny Jones to explain what demons truly are. The episode title calls him darker than Satan, a tag from his dark field of work. Gillis studies demon lore and case files of haunts.

Gillis argues demons are not the horned beasts of films but a class of being with rules of its own. He draws on old texts and his case work to build the claim. Jones asks how he sorts true cases from fraud and fear. Listeners get a cold, close look at a grim field. The library holds the talk as an archive record of his stated views.
podcast-joerogan-GuoglIuhNjY:
Actor and commentator Russell Brand tells Rogan, in a segment of the Joe Rogan Experience, that the veil is lifting on the corporate political system. Brand remade himself from film star into a media critic with a huge online following. His message is that power hides in plain sight.

He argues that big firms and governments now act as one machine, and that more people can see the seams than before. Rogan asks where the hope sits in that picture. The segment captures Brand's awakening narrative in his own fast, funny style, part sermon and part stand-up, aimed at listeners who feel the system is rigged.
